subject.title: fix(onboarding): skip setup for configured gateways and require inference first

question: After the startup defect and proof gap are resolved, should the onboarding, profile-migration, Codex-runtime, and dependency changes land together or be split by owner boundary?
rationale: These changes form a coherent route-binding design but affect independently sensitive compatibility and security surfaces; automation cannot choose the acceptable review and rollback unit.

options.title: Repair and land together
options.body: Keep the coherent design in one PR, requiring conflict resolution and exact-head proof for every retained compatibility-sensitive surface.

options.title: Split sensitive boundaries
options.body: Separate onboarding from profile migrations, Codex runtime identity, and dependency changes so each surface can be reviewed and rolled back independently.

options.title: Pause this landing candidate
options.body: Keep the linked issues open and replace this branch if conflict resolution leaves unrelated or unprovable churn.

recommendation.title: Repair and land together
recommendation.body: Keep the coherent design in one PR, requiring conflict resolution and exact-head proof for every retained compatibility-sensitive surface.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored and is assigned to the central implementation and owns the nearby current-main startup behavior.
